Incan is a statically typed programming language with Python-inspired readability and a Rust-backed native toolchain—being developed with a future of more inspectable, AI-assisted software development in mind.

01 / About Incan

A different balance between readability and precision.

Python shows how readable syntax can make software easier to author and understand. Rust brings static guarantees, native execution, and an established library ecosystem. Incan explores its own way of bringing these strengths together.

The goal is not simply to imitate either language. It is to build a coherent language and toolchain that keep application logic readable while making more of the underlying mechanics explicit and inspectable.

01 — AUTHORING

Readable by design

Python-inspired syntax aims to keep everyday application logic expressive and easy to follow.

02 — TYPES

Make structure explicit

Static typing and compiler feedback help developers understand program structure and errors.

03 — EXECUTION

Native applications

Incan's toolchain uses Rust to produce native binaries within the documented supported workflows.

04 — PROJECT MODEL

More to inspect

The project is working toward clearer relationships between source, dependencies, builds, and evidence.

04 / AI-first vision

Build software that people can inspect and verify.

Incan's longer-term vision is for developers and AI agents to work from a shared understanding of a project. Rather than treating generated code as the end result, the workflow should make it easier to examine proposed changes, understand their impact, run tests, and review evidence.

This direction informs the language, compiler feedback, project model, and tooling. It is an evolving vision: not every part of the described workflow is available today.

Explore the project website ↗
05 / The toolchain

Meet Oven.

Oven is the build and project system being developed around Incan and Rust. Its direction is to make project inputs and build outputs more explicit and inspectable, including dependencies, compiler versions, targets, and artifacts.

Current scope

Oven Alpha

Oven Alpha supports documented build, run, and test workflows without Cargo within a defined scope. Some preparation and compatibility-publishing workflows may still involve Cargo.

Important context

Experimental by design

Oven Alpha is experimental. Consult its current documentation before relying on a specific workflow, and distinguish implemented capabilities from planned architecture.

07 / Project status

Explore what exists today.

Incan is beta software. The 0.5 release line is available, and the language and toolchain continue to evolve. Some areas—including Oven Alpha and checked C interoperability—have explicitly experimental scopes.

Release and roadmap note: Roadmap items describe planned outcomes, not guaranteed release dates. Check the documentation, release notes, and compatible tutorial version before relying on a feature or using it in production.
0.5 line

Published release line with documented application workflows and tutorials.

0.6

Planned architectural work around compiler/backend cutover, Oven project authority, and foundations for self-hosting. Consult the latest project status for progress.

Beyond

Further language, ecosystem, investigation, runtime, and stabilization work is described in the project roadmap; milestones may change as development proceeds.
